headword: {更年期障害|こうねんきしょうがい}
reading: こうねんきしょうがい

definitions.explanation: The range of physical and emotional symptoms brought on by the hormonal changes of middle age — hot flashes, sweating, palpitations, irritability, insomnia. Used of women and, increasingly, of men as {男性|だんせい}{更年期障害|こうねんきしょうがい}.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}は{更年期障害|こうねんきしょうがい}に{悩|なや}んでいる。
examples.english: My mother is suffering from menopausal symptoms.

examples.japanese: {急|きゅう}に{汗|あせ}が{出|で}るのは{更年期障害|こうねんきしょうがい}の{症状|しょうじょう}かもしれない。
examples.english: Suddenly breaking into a sweat may be a symptom of menopause.

examples.japanese: {更年期障害|こうねんきしょうがい}は{我慢|がまん}するものではなく、{婦人科|ふじんか}で{相談|そうだん}すれば{治療|ちりょう}を{受|う}けられる。
examples.english: Menopausal symptoms are not something to be endured; if you consult a gynecologist, you can receive treatment.

notes:
{更年期|こうねんき} (the change of life, menopause) + {障害|しょうがい} (disorder, impairment). Note that {更年期|こうねんき} alone names the life stage; {更年期障害|こうねんきしょうがい} names the symptoms that trouble people during it.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {更年期障害|こうねんきしょうがい}の{症状|しょうじょう}: menopausal symptoms
- {更年期障害|こうねんきしょうがい}に{悩|なや}む: to suffer from menopausal symptoms
- {男性|だんせい}{更年期障害|こうねんきしょうがい}: male menopause

USAGE:
A neutral medical term, used freely in health articles and at the clinic. Applying it to someone else's bad mood ({更年期|こうねんき}じゃないの) is a well-known insult, so avoid it as a joke.
